transcript.text: Hi, I'm Sensei. Put your page under the camera and start solving. I'm watching.
You wrote v_y = 20 m/s, but the initial speed is 20 m/s at an angle. What part of the velocity is vertical?
All of it? The ball is going up at 20 meters per second, it says so in the question.
Okay, let me think.
The ball's speed is 20 m/s at an angle, so only part of that is vertical. What's the vertical part?
But it's launched upward, so it's going up at 20. The angle just tells you it's tilted.
Good question. One moment.
Imagine a ball launched straight up at 20 m/s. How long until it returns? Then think how the angle changes that.
Straight up would be 2 times 20 over 9.8, so 4.08. That's what I got. So the angle doesn't change anything.
Let me see.
You're thinking about the straight-up case, which is a good start. But the angle changes the vertical speed. Try again: what's the vertical part of 20 m/s at 60 degrees?
Why would it change though? It's still moving at 20 meters per second, just sideways a bit.
Got it. Give me a second.
The speed is 20 m/s, but only part of it is vertical. Try thinking about a 30-60-90 triangle to find the vertical part.
You keep saying only part is vertical but I don't see why. If it moves 20 a second, it goes up 20 a second.
Okay, let me think.
The speed is 20 m/s, but only part of it goes up. Think of a 30-60-90 triangle: at 60 degrees, the vertical part is 20 times sin(60).
That's just a formula. Why would the ball be slower going up than the 20 it was launched at?
Good question. One moment.
Imagine a ball thrown at 20 m/s straight up—its vertical speed is 20 m/s. Now throw it at 60 degrees—only part goes up. What’s the vertical speed if it’s 20 m/s at 60 degrees?
You keep asking the same thing. I still think it's 20, it says 20 in the question.
Let me see.
The speed is 20 m/s, but only part of it is going up. Try a smaller angle, like 30 degrees—what’s the vertical part then?
I dunno, I still don't get why it isn't just 20. I'm keeping 4.08.
Got it. Give me a second.
The vertical speed isn't 20 m/s because the ball is launched at an angle. Try a simpler case: if it were launched at 30 degrees, what would the vertical speed be?
